text: {"score":3,"justification":"The numbers match the card and the leaning (inconclusive) is cautious and sensible, with specific low-complexity claims and a good point about C0059583. But the summary contradicts itself and has a few unsupported statements, so an investigator would need to redo some of the reading. The next steps are generic and omit the targeted request the text promises.","problems":["The headline says 99215 is elevated 'in every complexity tier' and the text says 'two to four times the all-provider rate in every tier'. Tier ratios are about 3.1x, 3.3x, 2.6x, 2.8x, 3.7x and 2.0x, so 'two to four times' roughly holds. The rate is compared to the all-provider rate, not to expected, which is a loose basis.","The rationale says 'The billing pattern leans toward upcoding' while the leaning field is 'inconclusive'. This is internally inconsistent.","It says the mix is 'dominated by 99214', which is true (584 of 872), but it is irrelevant to the upcoding argument and unexplained.","The next_steps are generic: 'larger sample' with no specific claim IDs. The text promises a 'targeted records request for the low-complexity 99215 claims', but next_steps does not include it. Only 3 of 25 low-complexity claims are even cited, and C0059583 is not among the cited ids.","C0059583 is described as a 'supported claim' billed for abdominal pain with 51 minutes and high MDM, yet it is not cited in cited_claim_ids. Citing a below-billed 99214 note (C0059564) as an example in an upcoding summary is weak support.","The statement that the diagnosis codes 'would not usually support high-complexity decision making' is an unsupported clinical assertion. It also ignores that the z-score of 1.60 vs peers is modest and the 19 returned records (2.2%) are very few.","The text says 'all documented at high MDM' and that data-reviewed notes 'all match lab lines', which is trivial since the card shows 0 mismatches. It does not flag that minutes were recorded for only some of the documents."]}
